results.title: Spread at least $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has spread at least $k$, for a natural number $k$, when for every family $x_1, \dots, x_k$ of nontrivial elements of $G$, not necessarily distinct, there is an element $y \in G$ such that the subgroup $\langle x_i, y \rangle$ generated by $x_i$ and $y$ is all of $G$ for every $i$.

results.title: Spread exactly $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has spread exactly $k$, for a natural number $k$, when $G$ has spread at least $k$ and, for every natural number $m > k$, $G$ does not have spread at least $m$.

results.title: Existence of a group of spread exactly one (Kourovka 21.38)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conjecture that there exists a group of spread exactly $1$.

results.title: There is a group of spread exactly one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exists a group $G$ of spread exactly $1$: for every nontrivial $x \in G$ there is $y \in G$ with $\langle x, y \rangle = G$, but for every natural number $m > 1$ there are nontrivial elements $x_1, \dots, x_m \in G$ such that no single $y \in G$ satisfies $\langle x_i, y \rangle = G$ for all $i$. This answers Kourovka Problem 21.38 affirmatively.

results.title: Spread of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group. The spread $s(G)$ of $G$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of the natural numbers $k$ such that for any non-trivial elements $x_1, \dots, x_k$ of $G$ (not necessarily distinct) there exists $y \in G$ such that the subgroup $\langle x_i, y \rangle$ generated by $x_i$ and $y$ is all of $G$ for every $i$. In particular $s(G) = \infty$ when there is no largest such $k$.

results.title: Burness–Guralnick–Harper spread theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Then the spread $s(G)$ is at least $2$ if and only if every proper quotient of $G$ is cyclic, that is, $G/N$ is cyclic for every non-trivial normal subgroup $N$ of $G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 14.1
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every finite group $G$ with no nontrivial normal subgroup of odd order and every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ whose order is a power of $2$, if $\varphi$ fixes every element of some Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, then $\varphi^2$ is conjugation by some element of $G$, that is, $\varphi^2$ is an inner automorphism.

results.title: Glauberman's theorem on squares of $2$-automorphisms (Kourovka Problem 14.1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group with no nontrivial normal subgroup of odd order, and let $\varphi$ be an automorphism of $G$ whose order is a power of $2$. If $\varphi$ fixes every element of some Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, then $\varphi^2$ is an inner automorphism of $G$, that is, $\varphi^2$ is conjugation by some $g \in G$.

results.title: Order-preserving reindexing of columns preserves reduced row echelon form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a type with elements $0$ and $1$, and let $A$ be a matrix over $R$ in reduced row echelon form whose rows are indexed by a linearly ordered set and whose columns are indexed by a linearly ordered set $N$. Let $e : O \to N$ be an order isomorphism from a linearly ordered set $O$. Then the matrix $B$ with columns indexed by $O$ and entries $B_{ik} = A_{i\,e(k)}$ is in reduced row echelon form.

results.title: Existence of the reduced row echelon form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ and $n$ be finite linearly ordered sets, and let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over $K$. Then there are an $m \times n$ matrix $R$ over $K$ in reduced row echelon form and an invertible $m \times m$ matrix $P$ over $K$ with $R = PA$. In other words, $A$ is row-equivalent to a matrix in reduced row echelon form.

results.title: Uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ and $n$ be finite linearly ordered sets, and let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be $m \times n$ matrices over $K$ in reduced row echelon form. If $R_2 = P R_1$ for some invertible $m \times m$ matrix $P$ over $K$, then $R_1 = R_2$. In other words, a row-equivalence class contains at most one matrix in reduced row echelon form.

results.title: Invertible row operations preserve the null space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ and $n$ be finite sets, let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over $K$, and let $P$ be an invertible $m \times m$ matrix over $K$. Then the linear maps $x \mapsto PAx$ and $x \mapsto Ax$ on $K^n$ have the same kernel; that is, the homogeneous systems $PAx = 0$ and $Ax = 0$ have the same solutions.

results.title: Frobenius partitions with at most $k$ repetitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $\varphi_k(n)$ is the number of generalized Frobenius partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $k$ times in each row. results.title: Tiling of an abelian group by translates
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $F, A \subseteq G$. Then $F$ tiles $G$ with tiling set $A$ if the map $A \times F \to G$, $(a, f) \mapsto a + f$, is a bijection; equivalently, every element of $G$ lies in $a + F$ for exactly one $a \in A$.

results.title: Periodic tiling set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $A$ of an abelian group $G$ is periodic if there exist a subgroup $H$ of $G$ of finite index and a finite set $S \subseteq G$ such that $A = S + H$, that is, $A$ is the union of finitely many cosets of $H$.

results.title: Aperiodic tiling equation
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group. A set $F \subseteq G$ forms an aperiodic tiling equation if $F$ tiles $G$ with some tiling set $A \subseteq G$, and no tiling set $A \subseteq G$ with which $F$ tiles $G$ is periodic.

results.title: Greenfeld–Tao counterexample to the periodic tiling conjecture
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a finite abelian group $G_0$ and a finite non-empty set $F \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2 \times G_0$ that forms an aperiodic tiling equation in the group $\mathbb{Z}^2 \times G_0$.

results.title: Aperiodic tiling equations in high-dimensional integer lattices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $d_0$ such that for every natural number $d \ge d_0$ there exists a finite non-empty set $F \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ that forms an aperiodic tiling equation in $\mathbb{Z}^d$.

results.title: Continuous tiling of Euclidean space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $\sigma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ continuously tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ with tiling set $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ if for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure) there is exactly one $v \in \Lambda$ with $x \in v + \sigma$.

results.title: Periodic continuous tiling set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is periodic if there exist a lattice $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, that is, a discrete additive subgroup that spans $\mathbb{R}^d$ over $\mathbb{R}$, and a finite set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\Lambda = S + L$, so that $\Lambda$ is the union of finitely many cosets of $L$.

results.title: Aperiodic continuous tiling equation
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $\sigma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ forms an aperiodic continuous tiling equation if $\sigma$ continuously tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ with some tiling set $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, and no tiling set $\Lambda$ with which $\sigma$ continuously tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ is periodic.

results.title: Aperiodic continuous tiling equations in high-dimensional Euclidean space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $d_0$ such that for every natural number $d \ge d_0$ there exists a bounded measurable set $\sigma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of positive Lebesgue measure that forms an aperiodic continuous tiling equation.

The start states of a right-hand side $\beta$, a list of grammar symbols, for $q$ given $R$ are defined by recursion on $\beta$: for the empty right-hand side they are the one-element list $[q]$, and for a symbol $X$ followed by $\beta'$ they are the states of $D$, in order, at which $X$ fits given $R$ and the…

results.title: One round of the item search against a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, an encoded DFA $D$ and a list $R$ of natural numbers (the items found so far), one round produces the list of the codes $\langle A, \langle p, q \rangle \rangle$, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the natural-number pairing, for every production $A \to \beta$ of $g$, every state $q$ of $D$ and every start state $p$ of $\beta$ for $q$ given $R$.

results.title: Candidate items for a grammar and a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$, the candidate items form the list of the codes $\langle A, \langle p, q \rangle \rangle$, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the natural-number pairing, for every left-hand side $A$ of a production of $g$ (listed once per production) and all states $p$ and $q$ of $D$.

results.title: Items found for a grammar and a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$, the found items are the list obtained from the empty list by applying one round of the item search of $g$ and $D$ as many times as the length of the list of candidate items of $g$ and $D$.

results.title: The intersection-emptiness test for a grammar and a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded grammar with start nonterminal $S$, let $D$ be an encoded DFA with start state $s$, and write $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ for the natural-number pairing. The test of $g$ and $D$ is true exactly when there is no accepting state $f$ of $D$ that is also one of the states of $D$ and for which the code $\langle S, \langle s, f \rangle \rangle$ is among the found items of $g$ and $D$.

results.title: Start states of a right-hand side are states of the DFA
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, $R$ a list of natural numbers and $q$ one of the states of $D$. Then for every right-hand side $\beta$, every start state of $\beta$ for $q$ given $R$ is one of the states of $D$.

results.title: Sound items for a grammar and a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$, a natural number $x$ is a sound item when there are natural numbers $A$, $p$, $q$ and a word $w$ such that $x = \langle A, \langle p, q \rangle \rangle$, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the natural-number pairing, the nonterminal $A$ yields $w$ in the grammar denoted by $g$, and the automaton denoted by $D$, run on $w$ from state $p$, ends in state $q$.

results.title: Completeness of the start states in a DFA
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and $D$ an encoded DFA over an alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, and let $\rho$ be an encoded right-hand side whose decoding yields a word $u$ in the grammar that $g$ denotes. If $p$ is one of the states of $D$ and the automaton that $D$ denotes, run on $u$ from state $p$, ends in state $q$, then $p$ is a start state of $\rho$ for $q$ given the items found for $g$ and…

results.title: Correctness of the intersection-emptiness test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded grammar $g$ and every encoded DFA $D$, the intersection-emptiness test of $g$ and $D$ returns true if and only if the intersection of the language of $g$ and the language of $D$ is empty.

results.title: The inclusion test for a grammar and a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$ over the same alphabet $T$, where $T$ has decidable equality, the inclusion test on $g$ and $D$ is the Boolean value of the emptiness test on $g$ and the complement of $D$.

results.title: Correctness of the inclusion test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, every encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ and every encoded DFA $D$ over $T$, the inclusion test on $g$ and $D$ returns true if and only if the language of $g$ is contained in the language of $D$.

results.title: Emptiness of the intersection of a context-free and a regular language is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(g, D)$, where $g$ is an encoded context-free grammar over $T$ and $D$ is an encoded DFA over $T$, that the intersection of the language of $g$ and the language of $D$ is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine.

results.title: Inclusion of a context-free language in a regular language is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(g, D)$, where $g$ is an encoded context-free grammar over $T$ and $D$ is an encoded DFA over $T$, that the language of $g$ is contained in the language of $D$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine.

results.title: x-fast trie
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys consists of a finite set of stored keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$ together with, for each level $l \in \{0, \dots, w\}$, a finite set of natural numbers, intended to hold the $l$-bit prefixes of the stored keys.

results.title: Bit prefix of a key
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $l$ and $w$ and a $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$l$ prefix of $x$ is the natural number $\lfloor x / 2^{w-l} \rfloor$, where $w - l$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $l > w$). For $l \le w$ these are the top $l$ bits of $x$, a number below $2^l$.

results.title: The empty prefix is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$0$ prefix of $x$ (the trie root) is $0$.

results.title: The full-length prefix of a key is the key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$w$ prefix of $x$ equals $x$.

results.title: A prefix fits in its length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $l \le w$ and a $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$l$ prefix of $x$ is less than $2^l$.

results.title: Valid x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys is valid when, for every level $l \in \{0, \dots, w\}$, the level-$l$ set of $t$ equals the set of $l$-bit prefixes (top $l$ bits) of the stored keys of $t$.

results.title: The empty x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The empty x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys stores no keys, and the prefix set at each of its levels $0, 1, \dots, w$ is empty.

results.title: Insertion into an x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Inserting a $w$-bit key $x$ into an x-fast trie $t$ adds $x$ to the keys stored in $t$ and, for each level $0 \le l \le w$, adds the $l$-bit prefix of $x$ to the prefix set at level $l$.

results.title: The empty x-fast trie is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $w$, the empty x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, which has no stored keys and every level empty, is valid.

results.title: Insertion preserves validity of an x-fast trie
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t$ is a valid x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys and $x \in \{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$, then the x-fast trie obtained from $t$ by inserting $x$ is valid.

results.title: Keys of an x-fast trie after insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every $w$-bit key $x$, the set of keys stored in the trie obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ is the set of keys stored in $t$ with $x$ added.

results.title: Level probe of an x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys, a level $0 \le l \le w$ and a $w$-bit key $x$, the probe of level $l$ of $t$ at $x$ returns true exactly when the $l$-bit prefix of $x$ belongs to the prefix set stored at level $l$ of $t$.

results.title: Level probes of a valid x-fast trie
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, let $0 \le l \le w$ and let $x$ be a $w$-bit key. The probe of level $l$ of $t$ at $x$ succeeds if and only if some key $y$ stored in $t$ has the same $l$-bit prefix as $x$.

results.title: Membership query in an x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the membership query of $x$ in $t$ answers true exactly when the length-$w$ prefix of $x$, which is $x$ itself, lies in the prefix set that $t$ stores for level $w$: a single probe of the deepest level, as in the classical structure.

results.title: The membership test of a valid x-fast trie is exact
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a valid x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a $w$-bit key $x$, the membership test of $t$ at $x$, which probes the deepest level $w$, returns true if and only if $x$ is stored in $t$.

results.title: An inserted key passes the membership test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every $w$-bit key $x$, the membership test at $x$ of the trie obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ returns true.

results.title: Successor in an x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x \in \{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$, the successor of $x$ in $t$ is the least stored key of $t$ that is greater than $x$ when some stored key is greater than $x$; otherwise $x$ has no successor in $t$.

results.title: Predecessor query in an x-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the predecessor of $x$ in $t$ is the greatest key stored in $t$ that is smaller than $x$, if such a key exists; otherwise the query returns no key.

results.title: Characterization of the x-fast trie successor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be an x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys and let $x$ and $y$ be keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$. The successor of $x$ in $t$ exists and equals $y$ if and only if $y$ is a stored key of $t$, $x < y$, and $y \le z$ for every stored key $z$ of $t$ with $x < z$.

results.title: When an x-fast trie has no successor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the successor query of $x$ in $t$ returns no key if and only if no key stored in $t$ is greater than $x$.

results.title: Characterization of the x-fast trie predecessor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and keys $x, y < 2^w$, the predecessor query of $x$ in $t$ returns $y$ if and only if $y$ is stored in $t$, $y < x$, and every key $z$ stored in $t$ with $z < x$ satisfies $z \le y$.

results.title: When an x-fast trie has no predecessor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the predecessor query of $x$ in $t$ returns no key if and only if no key stored in $t$ is smaller than $x$.

results.title: y-fast trie skeleton
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A y-fast trie skeleton over $w$-bit keys consists of an x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, whose stored keys are the representatives, together with a bucket $B_r$, a finite set of keys, for every key $r \in \{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$.

results.title: Keys of a y-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $t$ be a y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, let $R$ be the set of keys stored in the representative x-fast trie of $t$, and for each $r \in R$ let $B(r)$ be the bucket owned by $r$. The set of keys stored in $t$ is the union of the buckets of its representatives, $\bigcup_{r \in R} B(r)$.

results.title: Membership in a y-fast trie via representatives' buckets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every y-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every $w$-bit key $x$, $x$ is stored in $t$ if and only if $x$ lies in the bucket owned by some representative of $t$, that is, by some key stored in the representative x-fast trie of $t$.

results.title: Valid y-fast trie skeleton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A y-fast trie skeleton $t$ over $w$-bit keys, with bucket $B_r$ owned by each key $r$, is valid when its representative x-fast trie is valid, a key $r$ is stored in the representative x-fast trie exactly when its bucket $B_r$ is nonempty, and every key $r$ stored in the representative x-fast trie lies in its own bucket $B_r$.

results.title: Representatives of a valid y-fast trie are stored keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a y-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys is valid, then every key of the representative x-fast trie of $t$ is a stored key of $t$.

results.title: Keys of a valid y-fast trie are the keys in buckets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t$ is a valid y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, then a $w$-bit key $x$ is stored in $t$ if and only if $x$ lies in the bucket owned by some $w$-bit key $r$ (such an owner $r$ is then necessarily a representative).
